May 3rd 2028

We have now moved on to Boddam Island. The island used to be inhabited by native Chagossians who gone over to set up plantations. However, they had been abandoned when they were forced out by the British. There had apparently been between 400 and 500 people who had lived there before the eviction. There had been a sizable settlement on Boddam Island which had now been lost to the jungles. It was eerie to walk through the abandoned streets, looking at how the schools, houses, shops and offices had been reclaimed by nature. There was also what appeared to be a farm, most likely for chickens. We later found what looked like a hen house. However, on closer inspection they were much bigger than a hen house would be expected to be. As we went further into the farm we found what looked to be a mound of dirt. It looked suspicious so we began to dig it up. We ended up finding some bones. At first glance it appears to be avian and it looks too big to be a chicken bone. We have arranged a full excavation for the near future.

May 12th 2028

The dig revealed more bones hidden deeper within the mound. It appeared to be an assortment of bones made up from several animals, not just a single one. The way they were all gathered in one spot suggests that it was a mass grave of some sort. Analysis is been run to determine the species of the bones. Meanwhile, we have continued to explore the rest of the Salomon Islands. From Boddam Island we then moved on to Takamaka Island and Fouquet Island

May 21st 2028

Analysis of the bones have found that they are the remains of dodos. It appears that the dodos were been kept on Boddam Island at some point, either as pets or even possibly as farm animals. This would explain the larger than usual hen house. This is intriguing news. While the dodo had been hunted and used as a source of food, this is the first evidence of them been bred and kept for this purpose. However, it is still unclear how the dodos arrived on the island. We have now finished our exploration of the Salomon Islands, and we now plan to move on to Peros Banhos. We intend build an outpost there due to its sheer size. I have already contacted Pierre, who has said he will get it built as soon as possible.

June 4th 2028

The construction of the second outpost on Peros Banhos is almost complete. Pierre has assured me that it will be completed by next week, the next 10 days at the latest. We have regrouped on Diego Garcia while we wait for the outpost to be built. Anna seems to have perked up a bit in the last few weeks which is nice to see, although she hasn't talked much to me and still seems to be avoiding me. She has been spending a lot of time with Hans recently though.

June 13th 2028

We received some bad news today. We found out that the Queen had passed away. It was a sad day considering Mauritius is a proud member of the Commonwealth. We had a small service and two minutes silence before we began work for the day. In honour of Queen Elizabeth we have decided to name the new outpost on Peros Banhos the 'Elizabeth's Outpost'. Elizabeth's Outpost has now been completed and we will move equipment to the island shortly. In the mean time we have been exploring the surrounding waters of the atoll. We came across an abandoned ship which had been run aground. Upon further inspection the boat seems to be from around the late 1600's. Inside we found some small wooden cages. Also among the wreckage I found what appears to be a traditional Chagossian nose flute. I put it in my pocket to examine later.

June 29th 2028

We have finally arrived on Peros Banhos. Elizabeth's Outpost looks fantastic and is great for our needs. We are currently located on Ile du Coine. From here we will be able to explore the atoll fully. It was previously home to another settlement and was where the coconut plantations were located. We will begin exploring the island within the next few days. I wonder if we will find any more evidence of dodo farming.
